definitions.critical_path_s: Bazel profile/BES critical path; wall time along the dependency path, not summed action work.
definitions.test_runner_worker_lifecycle_s: Sum over remote TestRunner actions of workerCompletedTimestamp - workerStartTimestamp. Aggregate concurrent worker-seconds, not user-visible elapsed time; includes the remote action worker's test setup and output phase.
definitions.test_runner_execution_wall_s: Sum of executionCompletedTimestamp - executionStartTimestamp for TestRunner actions; excludes input fetch and output upload.
definitions.test_runner_cpu_s: Sum of BuildBuddy usageStats.cpuNanos for TestRunner actions; CPU-seconds, not wall time.
definitions.queue_to_worker_start_s: Sum of workerStartTimestamp - queuedTimestamp; about 0.06s per action in both runs and not a material measured bottleneck.

sharding_experiment.cache_and_elapsed_caveat: Do not treat the 137.561s 4-to-8 invocation elapsed delta as causal: the second command reused the same Bazel server/output base; analysis phase fell from 63.671s to 1.517s, and the second run had only 12 newly executed actions. The 8 test actions did run fresh because --nocache_test_results was set. The action critical path and remote action timings are the more relevant comparison.

browser.question: Do merged 4-to-8 shard changes show a credible browser-test effect?

controlled_same_source_pair.design: Sequential forced 4-shard then 8-shard commands in one RBE runner/Bazel output base; both used --nocache_test_results, so every test shard action executed fresh. Same 41 test identities in each; 0 failures/skips.
controlled_same_source_pair.interpretation: Direct within-source evidence for lower critical browser-test time at higher aggregate worker/CPU cost. It is one ordered pair; second-run analysis was warm, so invocation elapsed delta is confounded. The fresh per-shard test actions and critical action are the relevant timing comparison.

fresh_eight_shard_ci_observations.result: 8/8 fresh remote actions passed; 41 test cases; 0 failures/skips.
fresh_eight_shard_ci_observations.source_comparison: Acceptance run for shard-count change on synthetic merge 79e575bc (base 9fc4b696, head ae627a32). This is a different source from the controlled pair, which used PR #9046 synthetic merge 05bb5682. Both reports count 41 cases, but identity-level equality was not verified.
Confounded follow-on: changed Agentplane evidence UI and test_thread_browser.py, and added three visual scenarios.
Confounded follow-on: changed pinned headless Chromium from 133 to 151 and updated its build/run dependencies.

history_cache_audit.note: BuildBuddy target history includes cached results attributed to newer commit SHAs. Its aggregate duration is summed shard runtime, not concurrent target wall time. Four sampled entries were cached and must not be counted as new timing observations.

conclusion.measured_effect: The one controlled fresh same-source pair improved critical-path browser time by 70.5s (31.1%) at +37.7% worker lifecycle and +36.2% test CPU. Three fresh 8-shard CI runs have 130.6-143.8s longest-shard times, versus three pre-change 4-shard CI profiles at 190.0-219.8s.
conclusion.statistical_claim: Promising, directionally consistent evidence; not statistically established. The controlled comparison has n=1 ordered pair. The acceptance run and the two extra fresh CI runs use different source/browser revisions; the latter were purposively sampled. Shards within one run are not independent samples. No defensible confidence interval or p-value.
limits: The successful post-change target-history page contains cached outputs; time values alone do not imply fresh execution.
The #9046 and #9122 fresh follow-on runs alter test or browser inputs, so they are not clean replications of the same workload.
End-to-end PR feedback time has multiple parallel gates and is not an estimate of this isolated target effect.

keepwarm.title: Landed keep-warm effect: runner probes and actual Bazel test phase

source_change.change: deletes the explicit `bazel shutdown` immediately before the test/build phase after impacted-target selection.

small_cached_test_phase_cohort.definition: Successful Bazel test phase, 1-10 impacted test targets, and `Executed 0 out of N tests` where N equals the target count; compare observed server PID changed versus retained.
small_cached_test_phase_cohort.interpretation: Descriptive association only: small unbalanced cached cohort (median target count6 versus2); exact label matching was not established by this extraction.

uncertainty_and_limits: No defensible causal confidence interval for production time savings from this observational slice: PRs and source revisions differ, no randomized crossover and exact target matching has not been established, and the execution cache and runner reuse state vary over time.

The direct mechanism result is much stronger than the wall-time estimate: 28 measured middle-window test phases changed server PID after target selection, while the PR #9069 exact-head test plus all 56 measured post-merge test phases retained the PID; this is evidence that the intended warm-server mechanism ran.

The small cached phase cohort gives a large raw timing contrast, but target-count distribution is different and exact test-label signatures do not overlap; it must not be generalized to production-average savings or treated as a formal effect interval.

One middle failure (23 impacted tests; 18 executed, 1 failing target; 321.793s Bazel elapsed, 281.43s critical path) emitted a before-test PID but failed before after-test probe. Preserve it as a pre-change control-period failure with unobserved restart outcome, not as a fast or successful phase.

Four post-merge successful jobs (run/PR IDs 37260884786/#9111, 37261629700/#9115, 37266122971/#9132, 37266287806/#9133) were legitimate zero-target no-ops: each explicitly reported affected targets: 0, skipped test/build, and exited 0. They have no actual test-phase measurement and are excluded only from driver timing samples, while retained in period totals. The //external diagnostics also appear in runs that do execute tests, so they are not the explanation for these no-ops.

The treatment is a one-line Bazel driver change. Other repository/Bazel/test diffs, runner reuse, remote and disk-cache state, target selection volume, failures, and day-specific load remain confounders. Critical path describes remote action critical path, not local Bazel server analysis time.

nix_wheel_checkout.limits: Observed component-step reduction, with post source refs carrying the shallow-checkout config and successful source verification. It does not establish the same reduction in full CI time; step times are rounded to seconds and cohorts are observational.

galaxy_role_provisioning.selector: Skip Galaxy role cache restore/install/save only when a pull request is proven unrelated; retain setup for ansible/**, Ansible config, pushes, manual runs, and unknown selection.
galaxy_role_provisioning.comparison: Before the change, all 43 available pre-commit jobs were eligible unrelated changes but ran role restore/install. After, all 89 eligible unrelated jobs skipped all three role steps. One after-period change to .pre-commit-config.yaml correctly retained role setup.
galaxy_role_provisioning.observed_component_time: Executed role setup steps averaged 1.28 seconds per pre-change head (median 1 second, range 0–2); post eligible jobs have zero executed role-step time. GitHub timestamps are rounded to whole seconds and roles were already cached, so this confirms the skip behavior but supports only a small runtime reduction estimate.
galaxy_role_provisioning.whole_job_context: The complete pre-commit job did not shorten in these cohorts: eligible median durations were 129 seconds before, 137.5 in middle, and 134 after. These totals include setup, caches, changed-file checks, and file-dependent hooks; they do not isolate this change.
galaxy_role_provisioning.limits: Direct step conclusions show activation. Do not infer overall PR/CI improvement from the Galaxy change in this warm-cache sample.
